id.description: Same as the file name without .yaml. Never change it once merged: links use it.

caliber.description: Id of the caliber, which is also the folder name: 556-nato, 300-blk, 9mm-luger, 762x39, 308-win, 65-creedmoor.

brand.description: Maker, for factory loads. Leave out for generic and military-spec types such as M193.

name.description: Full name, as the maker writes it plus the bullet weight and type.

short.description: Compact name for tables and printed targets, 32 characters at most.

sku.description: Product codes printed on the box, so a search for them finds the load.

standard.description: For a factory load that stands in for a common type (e.g. Federal Gold Medal 168 gr for ".308 168 gr match"): that type's name.

sameAs.description: Id of the standard type this factory load is made to, e.g. m193 or m855.

bc.description: Ballistic coefficient for the drag model below.

dragModel.description: Drag table the BC refers to.

platform.description: The upper the load is usually fired from; sets the default rail-to-bore height (ar15 for AR-15-size receivers, ar10 for AR-10-size).

confidence.description: high: the load's own chronograph series across barrel lengths. medium: measured at a couple of lengths, a similar load's curve fills the rest. low: one reading or only the maker's rating.

mvByBarrel.description: [barrel length in, muzzle velocity fps] pairs, shortest barrel first.

notes.description: How the numbers were measured or derived, and anything a reader should know about them.

anyOf.description: Id of a shared source in data/sources.yaml.

label.description: What the source is: publisher, title and year, e.g. "LuckyGunner .223/5.56 barrel length test (2026)".

url.description: Link to the source. Leave out only for print sources such as a field manual.

sources.description: Where the numbers came from: ids from data/sources.yaml, or { label, url }.
